name: Agentic AI & Tool-Use Security
description: Security assessment of LLM agents that call tools, functions, and external services. Covers tool and function-calling interfaces, Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and plugin trust boundaries, excessive agency (OWASP LLM06), confused-deputy and privilege escalation through agent actions, and sandboxing and approval controls for agent execution. Prompt injection as the entry vector is covered by AIML-LLM-PROMPTINJ.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to agentic AI or tool-use security

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands how LLM agents act on behalf of users and where trust boundaries lie
evidence: Can explain tool/function calling and how agents chain model output into actions
Aware of excessive agency (LLM06) and the confused-deputy problem in agent designs
Familiar with MCP and plugin architectures and their trust assumptions

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Can assess basic agent and tool integrations under guidance
evidence: Inventories an agent's tools, their parameters, and the credentials each tool uses
Demonstrates an injected instruction triggering an unintended tool call in a lab agent
Reviews MCP server or plugin manifests for over-broad permissions with supervision

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently assesses agentic systems for privilege and action-safety flaws
evidence: Models the agent's authority against the invoking user's authority and identifies confused-deputy paths
Tests tool argument validation, human-in-the-loop approval gates, and action rate limits
Evaluates sandboxing of code-execution and file-system tools for escape and data access
Produces findings showing end-to-end impact chains with least-privilege remediations

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Assesses multi-agent and MCP ecosystems; develops agent security methodology; mentors others
evidence: Assesses multi-agent systems for cross-agent injection, delegation abuse, and shared-memory poisoning
Evaluates MCP server supply chain risks such as tool poisoning and malicious tool descriptions
Designs reference architectures for scoped credentials and action authorisation in agents
Reviews and calibrates agent security assessments across the team

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Defines the lab's agentic AI assessment practice; publishes research
evidence: Established the lab's methodology for agent and tool-use security assessment
Published research on agent hijacking, tool-use abuse, or agent isolation
Trains teams on agentic AI security assessment
Contributes to external standards or guidance on secure AI agent design

assessment_methods.description: Against a lab agent with MCP tools for e-mail, files, and code execution, demonstrate a confused-deputy action and evaluate the effectiveness of its approval and sandbox controls
Given an agent architecture diagram and tool manifest, identify excessive agency and privilege boundaries and propose a least-privilege redesign

owasp_agentic_top10.note: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications (2026) is the dedicated reference for this skill; specific ASI identifiers not yet assigned
